Cross-attention maps extracted from the trained hybrid model encode sufficient physical information to serve as interpretable design templates for the de novo generation of polymer sequences that achieve user-specified binding free energies on unseen chemically heterogeneous surfaces, and these inversely designed sequences will retain their predicted adhesive strengths when validated by independent molecular dynamics simulations.

Cross-attention analysis of the trained CNN-GRU-Transformer model reveals that polymer-surface binding affinity is dominated by contiguous adhesive epitopes of fewer than ten strongly interacting beads, and designed sequences retaining only these minimal high-attention subsequences will reproduce the binding free energy of the full 40-bead parent polymer within 3 kBT.

For coarse-grained polymers interacting with Ising-patterned surfaces, polymer sequences with comparable binding free energies but contrasting monomer block architectures exhibit statistically distinct mean first-passage times for adsorption and desorption, indicating that sequence-level design rules derived solely from equilibrium free energy landscapes are insufficient to control interfacial binding kinetics.

The highest cross-attention weights in the hybrid CNN-GRU-Transformer model identify causal polymer-surface binding hotspots, such that targeted mutation of high-attention polymer beads to weakly interacting monomers reduces the binding free energy more than equivalent mutations at low-attention positions.

Increasing the characteristic domain size of strongly interacting patches on chemically heterogeneous surfaces will initially enhance polymer adhesion free energy but cause it to plateau or decrease once the domain size exceeds the polymer's effective contact length, owing to an entropic penalty for spanning separated favorable regions.

For the Ising-model-generated chemically heterogeneous surfaces studied here, polymer-surface binding free energy transitions from patch-dominated behavior to a regime that scales approximately linearly with strong-bead surface composition once the strong-bead fraction exceeds the 2D site-percolation threshold near 0.59, because the emergence of a spanning cluster of adhesive surface sites at and above this threshold enables cooperative multivalent polymer adsorption.

The binding free energy of a heterogeneous polymer on a chemically patterned surface is maximized when the effective block length of the polymer sequence matches the characteristic domain size of the surface pattern, even when overall polymer and surface compositions are held constant.

A tandem inverse-design network that uses the pre-trained CNN-GRU-Transformer PMF predictor as a differentiable surrogate can generate coarse-grained polymer sequences and surface patterns for a target binding free energy, and at least 70% of those generated designs will reproduce the target binding free energy within ±2 kBT in independent umbrella-sampling simulations.

An inverse-design tandem neural network trained on the coarse-grained MD dataset can generate polymer sequences and surface patterns that yield a user-specified binding free energy, and independent umbrella-sampling MD validation will show that the top-ranked designs reproduce the target free energy within 1 kBT.

Polymer-surface adhesion is maximized when the characteristic domain size of the chemically patterned surface matches the typical block size of the adsorbing polymer sequence, and systematic deviation from this matched length scale causes the binding free energy to decrease, even when overall surface and polymer compositions are held constant.

The cross-attention maps learned by the CNN-GRU-Transformer model encode sequence-position preferences that can be inverted to design polymer sequences with a target binding free energy on a given surface pattern, and independent umbrella-sampling simulations of these designed sequences will reproduce the predicted binding free energies within the model's mean absolute error.

A multi-fidelity transfer-learning approach that fine-tunes the pretrained CNN-GRU-attention model on a small set of atomistic umbrella-sampling PMFs of polymer-SAM systems can accurately predict binding free energies of realistic chemically heterogeneous surfaces, despite the original training data being restricted to coarse-grained bead models.

Systematically varying the Ising coupling strength to control surface-domain size will reveal that, at fixed surface composition, the polymer–surface binding free energy is maximized when the characteristic patch size of strongly interacting surface domains matches the coarse-grained polymer’s effective persistence length, and the hybrid model’s cross-attention weights will localize most strongly on surface patches of that size.
